BRENT calendar spreads have swung into a ferocious backwardation as attacks on shipping escalate around the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia’s oil installations on the Red Sea are hit by missiles and drones launched from Yemen. The six-month futures spread is trading in a backwardation of $15 per barrel up from flat or a small contango at the start of July before the ceasefire between Iran and the United States broke down. Traders increasingly anticipate a prolonged disruption of exports from around the Persian Gulf that will tighten crude inventories through the end of the year and into 2027:

#Gold holds near USD 4,400, having traded as high as USD 4,442 during the Asian session, with the market caught between renewed strength in crude oil, rising bond yields and a softer dollar. Ongoing Gulf tensions are keeping oil prices volatile, and today’s renewed strength is feeding into higher inflation expectations and Treasury yields, weighing on bullion. Algorithmic trading is likely amplifying this relationship, with the negative yield impact only partly offset by dollar weakness, particularly against the Japanese yen.

Beyond these short-term cross-market moves, most developments this week are likely to remain sideshows ahead of the US CPI and PPI releases, which will be critical in shaping expectations for the Fed’s September meeting. Meanwhile, underlying demand remains supported by central-bank buying, with the People’s Bank of China adding the most gold to its reserves since 2023 in August, marking a 22nd consecutive month of purchases.

#Commodities
#Copper on the LME extended gains, hitting a record high for a second straight session at USD 14624.5 per tons, supported by persistent market tightness as miners struggle to keep pace with robust demand heading into the annual peak-demand season. Tightness has been exacerbated by large flows of refined metal to the US ahead of a potential tariff announcement. Copper has gained 17% this year, underpinned by a longer-term mismatch between constrained mine supply and growing demand from data centres, renewable energy infrastructure and power grids.

#Crudeoil holds most of last week’s strong gain, with Brent briefly topping USD 98 a barrel on Monday, a six-week high. Iran said an accord with Oman is imminent and will include a temporary safe shipping route, raising questions about how the US may respond after striking Iranian tankers over the weekend. Tehran also warned that vessels face the risk of attack near Oman, highlighting the continued uncertainty surrounding regional shipping and supply flows.

#Wheat futures rebounded on signs Russia remains committed to continuing its war in Ukraine, heightening concerns about prolonged disruptions to grain shipments from the Black Sea. Prices slumped from a three-year high last week ahead of weekend talks between US envoys and President Vladimir Putin on Ukraine, but the meetings ended without any sign of progress
